readMe.title: China Defense-Industrial Atlas — Supplier Scorecards v1.2
readMe.blurb: Additive, source-gated supplier × capability assessments through 2026-08-31. This workbook preserves the legacy Atlas as context and does not replace its broader research-priority ranking.

notes.note: The unit of analysis is a supplier × capability family, not a corporate family or product brand. A parent’s strategic importance does not make every affiliate a technical supplier.

Systemic importance combines criticality, production maturity, cross-domain leverage, and technical frontier. The evidence-qualified lower bound discounts weaker evidence. It is a research triage score—not spend, valuation, targeting value, or sanctions advice.
Criticality 4 requires explicit sole/limited-source or requalification language. Only scores supported by that threshold receive a substitution-risk assessment; blank means unknown, not low risk.

Completed production-enabling awards (robotics, test, CNC, validation) are separated from mission-component suppliers. A shipyard robotics award is meaningful industrial-base evidence, not proof of a weapons-subsystem relationship.

PLA candidate notices, company marketing, and comparative tests are preserved as watchlist evidence. They do not enter the verified leaderboard until a final award, delivery, qualification, or other stronger evidence is found.
Foreign-dependency rows are tagged by directness and currentness. Historical export-control cases are not silently converted into current defense-program vulnerabilities.
For the full claim ledger and source detail, use the accompanying v1.2 SQLite database or the Atlas site’s Supplier scorecards tab.

bibliography.title: Bibliographic essay — what the new sources can prove
bibliography.blurb: A guide to the evidentiary division of labor behind the v1.2 supplier scorecards.

records.what_it_is_good_for: Named product categories, batch production, customer class, qualifications, capacity, and sometimes limited-source language.
records.what_it_cannot_prove_alone: A generic ‘special market’ disclosure does not identify a program, military buyer, monopoly, or delivery event.

records.what_it_is_good_for: Named winner, buyer, project scope, result state, date, and disclosed price for specific production or equipment procurements.
records.what_it_cannot_prove_alone: A shipyard production-equipment award does not establish a weapon component relationship or enterprise-wide revenue.

records.what_it_is_good_for: Demand shape, technical requirements, bid/pre-award/final-state distinctions, and named component stacks.
